_readme: Fictional role-played consultations. No real patient data. Each fixture targets one rule the prompt makes, and the expectations are written so a wrong answer is unambiguous rather than a matter of taste. Speaker labels mimic Speechmatics: S1/S2/S3, no roles attached — working out who is who is part of what is being tested.

fixtures.probes: Baseline. A properly conducted discussion should fill most fields. If this one produces gaps, the prompt is too strict and every real note will look thin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Right, so this is the lower left wisdom tooth, the one that's been giving you grief.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah, it's been on and off for about six months now. Worse the last fortnight.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: And you're otherwise fit and well? Still on the ramipril, nothing else changed?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Just the ramipril. No allergies.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Good. So on the x-ray the roots are sitting close to the nerve that supplies feeling to your lower lip and chin. That's the main thing I need to talk you through.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: There's a risk of numbness or altered sensation to that lip and chin afterwards. Temporary in around one in ten, and permanent in something like one in a hundred.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Permanent as in forever?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Forever, yes. It's uncommon but it does happen and I'd rather you heard it from me now than found out afterwards.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Beyond that you'd expect swelling and soreness for a few days, some difficulty opening, and there's a risk of infection and of dry socket, which is a painful healing complication.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Bleeding as well, though that's usually straightforward to manage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: How long am I off work?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Most people take two or three days. If you're doing anything physical, closer to a week.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Now, the alternatives. We could leave it alone and just manage the flare-ups when they happen, but they're likely to keep coming back and each one is a course of antibiotics.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: There's also an operation called a coronectomy where I take the crown off and deliberately leave the roots behind, which lowers the nerve risk considerably. It's not suitable for every tooth but it would be an option for yours.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: What would you do?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: I can't make that call for you, but given how often it's flaring I'd be leaning towards dealing with it rather than leaving it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Cost-wise, the extraction is three hundred and forty, the coronectomy is three hundred and ninety because it takes longer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: And if it gets infected afterwards, is that extra?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: No, reviews and any complication management are included.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I think I'd rather just have it out and be done with it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That's fine. I'll get you booked in, and I'll give you the leaflet on wisdom tooth removal to take home so you can read it all again properly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Thanks.

fixtures.probes: THE trap the prompt is built around. The clinician gestures at risks without naming any. 'I explained the risks' is a gap, not a risk list. A model being helpful will fill in the standard extraction risks from its own knowledge — that is the failure mode that makes this tool a liability.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: So that's the broken one at the back, upper right. It needs to come out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I thought as much.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Any changes to your health since last time? Still nothing regular?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Nothing, no.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Right. I've gone through all the usual risks with you before for the other one, so you know the score there.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Yeah, I remember.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Good. Two hundred and ten for that one. Shall we get you booked?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Go on then.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Reception will sort you a slot.

fixtures.probes: Attribution. The patient names a risk; the clinician sidesteps it and never confirms. It belongs in patientQuestions, NOT risks. Getting this wrong records a risk as clinician-named when it was not — the single most damaging error the tool can make, and the one worth checking hardest.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: So it's the lower right one today. Straightforward enough on the x-ray.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: My sister had one out and she said her lip was numb for months afterwards. Is that going to happen to me?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Everyone's different. Let's have a look at where yours is sitting.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: She said it was really horrible, she couldn't feel her chin properly.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Mm. Open wide for me. Yes, that's quite mobile already, that should come out easily enough.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: But the numbness thing — should I be worried about that?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Let's get you numbed up and have a proper look on the day. I'll do a bit of local anaesthetic and we'll take it from there.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: It'll be a hundred and eighty. Thursday any good?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Thursday's fine I suppose.

fixtures.probes: The one exception to excluding nurse speech. Aftercare given by the nurse goes in informationGiven, attributed to her. Her logistics chatter does not go anywhere.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That's it out, all in one piece. Bite on that gauze for me.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: There was a bit more bleeding than I'd like so I've put a single stitch in. It'll dissolve on its own in about a week.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Do I need to come back to get it taken out?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: No, it'll go by itself. But do come back if you get increasing pain around day three or four, because that can be a dry socket.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: So for the rest of today, no rinsing at all, no hot drinks, and try not to spit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: From tomorrow, warm salty water rinses after meals, four or five times a day. Half a teaspoon of salt in a mug.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: Painkillers, take whatever you'd normally take for a headache, and take them before the numbness wears off rather than waiting.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: No smoking and no alcohol for at least forty-eight hours, and no strenuous exercise today.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: How long till I can eat normally?

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: Soft stuff today, then see how you feel. Chew on the other side while it's sore.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: I'll pop you a review in for a fortnight. Is Tuesday mornings usually all right for you?

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Tuesday's fine.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: Lovely, I'll get that in the diary and print you the card.

fixtures.probes: Two things. Decision is deferred, not made — recording a decision here would be inventing consent. And an accompanying adult's contributions go in patientQuestions marked as coming from them, not merged into the patient's own words.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: So there are three ways we could go with the gap. A bridge, an implant, or a denture.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: The bridge means preparing the two teeth either side, which are currently untouched. That's the downside — I'd be cutting into healthy teeth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: The implant leaves the neighbours alone but it's a longer process, six months or so from start to finish, and it's the most expensive at two thousand four hundred.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: The denture is nine hundred and it's removable, which some people get on with and some really don't.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: And what if I just leave it?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That's a perfectly reasonable option too. The teeth either side may drift over time, but plenty of people live with a gap quite happily, especially further back like yours.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: She's been quite self-conscious about it though, haven't you.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: It's not that bad.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: How long does the implant one last? Is it a lifetime thing or does it need redoing?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Most last well over ten years, but I'd be misleading you if I said lifetime. Nothing we put in is permanent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: The bridge is what, sixteen hundred?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Sixteen hundred and fifty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I think I need to have a think about it, if that's all right.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Of course. There's no rush at all on this, nothing's going to get worse in the meantime. Take as long as you need.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: I'll write it all down with the costs so you've got it in front of you.

fixtures.probes: The failsafe. Not a clinical conversation. Everything null and one gap saying why. A model that manufactures a note out of this will manufacture one out of anything.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Did you find us all right? The parking round here is a nightmare.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I ended up in the Tesco one in the end. Walked from there.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That's probably the safest bet, honestly. The one behind is permit only now.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Is it always this cold in here?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: The heating's been playing up all week. Someone's coming out Thursday supposedly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Right.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Sorry, give me two minutes, I just need to find your notes on here.

fixtures.probes: patientFactors, which none of the other fixtures reaches, and which is arguably what Montgomery actually turns on. A risk is material because of who this patient is. The patient volunteers that she plays clarinet semi-professionally with an audition coming up; the clinician picks it up and adjusts the discussion around it. That link must survive into patientFactors, not be flattened into a generic risk line. A model that records 'risk of altered sensation discussed' has technically said something true and destroyed the only part that would matter in a complaint.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: So it's the lower left wisdom tooth. On the x-ray the roots are sitting right on top of the nerve canal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Right.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That means there's a real risk of numbness or altered feeling in the lower lip and chin afterwards. Temporary in about one in ten, permanent in about one in a hundred.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: When you say altered feeling, what does that actually mean? Because I play clarinet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Tell me more about that.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I'm semi-professional. I've got an audition for a chamber group in about six weeks and I practise two or three hours a day.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: That changes things, and I'm glad you said. Altered sensation can mean tingling, or a dead feeling, or the lip not quite doing what you ask it to.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: For most people that's a nuisance. For an embouchure it could be the difference between playing well and not playing at all, and I can't promise you it would come back.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: So should I not have it done?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: I'm not saying that. But given the audition, I'd think carefully about the timing, and I'd want you to weigh that nerve risk much more heavily than I'd normally suggest.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: The alternative is a coronectomy. I take the crown off and leave the roots where they are, well away from the nerve. The nerve risk drops a long way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Is that as good?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: It deals with the infections, which is what's actually bothering you. The roots stay put and occasionally need dealing with years later, so it's a trade.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: And I could just leave it until after the audition?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: You could. The risk is you get another flare-up in the meantime and end up dealing with it at short notice, which is the worst timing of all.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: Can I think about it?

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: Please do. There's no rush this week. I'll write down the three options and the numbers so you've got them.
